title: The Slot Without an Edge
concept: Under Alaska's current rules a records request can be spoken out loud and can't be refused for skipping the form. On November 11th the Department of Administration posted proposed changes, and per the Juneau Empire the draft would bar requests filed through third party services or automated tools, including AI, let agencies require their own forms or portals, stop work at 250 documents or 15 staff hours, charge for all of it once past five hours a month, cut the appeal window from 60 to 30 working days and give residents priority over nonresidents. Nothing reported says why the AI line is there. Drawn as a faceless gunmetal letterbox in a Juneau door with a pencilled DRAFT template on tracing vellum clipped beside it whose fourth edge is dashed, AUTOMATED TOOL = ?. A service envelope and a courier robot wait at the pencil line, a person drafts with an AI helper and carries the note to the slot where it stays half in, the night clerk gets the fair case, and in a door cross-section a stack of hand-filled forms meets the 250 line beside a dashed ghost IF ALLOWED. The film ends on the question of where a tool ends.

divergence_note: The last films were high-noon white sea ice with cobalt leads and a survey camera (11-14), a brass faucet with a face on an overcast pewter-sage gravel lot (11-13), a survey stake tag on rose dusk snow with a raven (11-12) and a vermilion take-a-number machine on a violet shore (11-10). This film is full night at one Juneau door, one sodium lamp, a FACELESS gunmetal letterbox, and the proposed rule drawn as graphite pencil on clipped tracing vellum with dashed edges and pencilled bolts, never hardware. The people (a requester and a night clerk) carry the feeling. Honest overlaps: 11-13 was also wet and had a metal fixture as its hero with a face and a two-accent grammar (mint AI, tomato rule), answered here by night, no face on the fixture, pencil-grey for the rule and ice-cyan only on screens for AI. 11-14 had a plate on its hero and two equal signs, answered by a template that is visibly a draft and a cross-section where one stack is only a dashed ghost. 11-10 had a machine that dispenses, so the letterbox only receives.

treatment.title: The Slot Without an Edge
treatment.summary: Dramatist winner 'The Slot Without an Edge', restaged after Gates 0B to 0D. A FACELESS gunmetal letterbox in the street door of a state office in Juneau on a rain-black night has always taken any question, even a spoken balloon. The proposed rule is a sheet of tracing vellum clipped beside the slot, a pencilled form-shaped outline whose fourth edge is a dashed line, pencilled bolt circles, a DRAFT tab and a BLANK hang tag. A service envelope and Tote the courier robot stop and wait at the pencil line (the reported verb, submitting through), a person drafts with an ice-cyan phone helper, fixes its mistake and carries the note to the slot where it presses at the dashed edge, neither in nor out. The crane through the slot shows the volume caps as a DRAFT tape line, a candle and an hour meter. Two same-size cards on the railing hold the residents draft and the statute's words, level, no verdict. The night clerk works the stack in a warm room for the fair case. The signature is the door in cross-section: one real stack stops at the 250 line beside a dashed ghost of Tote's, labelled VOLUME, A KNOWN PERSON and WHAT DOES THE TOOL LINE ADD?. The button holds the balloon at the threshold.
treatment.judge_reasoning: Dramatist pitch won (47 of 60): the only retention plan with every loop explicit and legal, an Act 3 that is a real test where the clerk's case gets its own scene and then both same-size envelopes stop at the same 250 line, an AI presence that only submits through (the reported verb), and the falsifier drawn on screen. Grafts: the Enthusiast's honest AI drafting upside with the person fixing the helper's mistake and carrying it to the slot, the Explainer's crane through the slot and VOLUME label, the Comedian's statute (now on a level card, not carved). Restaged at Gate 0: faceless letterbox, the rule as a pencilled draft, nothing shown admitted or refused.

angle.thesis: As the Juneau Empire reports it, Alaska's draft records rule would police how a request arrives instead of how much work it makes, and since its own caps already limit the work whatever tool filed it, the line it draws around AI needs a definition and a reason the public hasn't been shown.
supporting_facts: Today's rules don't care about the channel: a spoken request is valid and an agency can't deny one for skipping its form (c4, c5), and state law says every person has a right to inspect a public record, with exceptions (c16).

The draft adds a channel rule where there wasn't one: no requests submitted through third party services or automated tools, including AI, and agencies could require their own forms or portals (c2, c3, PROPOSED, per Juneau Empire).

The same draft already limits volume directly: stop at 250 documents or 15 staff hours, pay for all hours once past five a month, no copies of whole databases, reject requests for commercial gain (c6, c7, c13, c17), and no source gives any reason for the AI clause.
angle.counterpoint_to_honor: The agency's fair case, at full strength and in its own scene: records staff hours are finite, the department's stated aim is efficiency at no added cost (c19, a general aim, never presented as the AI clause's reason), the 10 working day clock is unchanged (c12), the public interest fee waiver stays (c9), and a state can sensibly want an accountable person on the other end of every request through one known channel (c3), which also makes the commercial gain and personal information screens (c13, c14) workable.
angle.falsifier: The thesis is false if the proposed regulation text (not yet readable, notice 225838 returns 403) defines 'automated tool' narrowly, for example bulk filing with no human involved, so that a person who drafts with AI and submits through the official portal is plainly allowed, or if the department shows a flood of machine-filed requests the 250 document and 15 hour caps couldn't handle.
angle.second_movement: The AI clause isn't the whole draft. Recontextualise it with the rest of the package: caps, all-hours fees, a shorter appeal window (60 to 30 working days, c10, c11) while the agency's 10 day clock stays put, resident priority (c15) beside the statute's 'every person' (c16). The test scene gives the agency its full case, then asks the narrow question: what does the tool line do that the caps don't?

runner_ups.angle: A (AI-first): the line moves from what a citizen asks to what a citizen used, the wrong place to draw it.
runner_ups.why_lost: Cross-challenge: B and C showed 'wrong place' is a verdict the record can't carry, since the text may define the term narrowly and 'submitting through' may not reach AI drafting. Kept its strongest picture, AI help makes a narrower request, as a stated upside, not a ruling.

runner_ups.angle: B (agency's fair case): most of the draft is a coherent workload trade, and only the AI clause goes unexplained.
runner_ups.why_lost: Cross-challenge: A noted it undersells that the caps make the tool line redundant for volume, and C that 'coherent' credits caps the film can't evaluate. Its fair case became the Act 3 test scene and its appeal-window asymmetry joined the second movement.

runner_ups.angle: C (structural): the draft changes the question from what you ask to how it arrives without saying where 'automated tool' ends.
runner_ups.why_lost: Won on falsifiability and became the spine, with A's upside and B's fair case grafted in. A challenged it as too dry for two minutes, answered by drawing the channel as a physical slot the film can watch.

angle.cross_challenge: One full round run by the showrunner across the three cards. A to B: credulous on 'efficiency' for the caps. B to A: booster in calling the line wrong before the text is seen. C to both: 'submitting through' is not 'drafted with', so neither may say the state bans AI help. A to C: a missing definition is a footnote unless the film shows why it touches a real person. Resolution: the thesis is a question with a falsifier, the upside is drawn honestly, the fair case gets a scene.
guardrails: Every draft provision is spoken PROPOSED or DRAFT and attributed to the Juneau Empire at least once per group.
Never give a reason for the AI clause, never tie c19 to it.
Never say the state bans AI help or AI drafting; the reported words are 'submitting through'.
Never call the residency priority or anything else illegal; show the statute's words beside the draft and stop.
Never say the first five hours are free today; five hours is the fee trigger in state law.
No comment deadline, no named official, never say the rule copies HB 377.

hook.frame1: Rain streaks through one sodium lamp cone onto a dark door and a faceless gunmetal letterbox, a cream question balloon drifts in from the dark, and a pencil starts sketching a dashed outline beside the slot.
hook.headline: ASK OUT LOUD · IT COUNTS
hook.loopback: Frame 1 is the question balloon drifting into the lamp cone toward the letterbox, the last image is the same balloon holding beside the person's note at the threshold between the open slot and the dashed pencil edge, neither in nor out.

open_loop.what: Why is the AI line there? Planted as a BLANK tag folded behind a clip on the draft template as it lands, dropped open under NOTHING REPORTED SAYS WHY, held on as the voice says hold on to that, kept in frame on the template in shots 4, 7 and 14 and spilling its glow in shot 8, paid when the same tag swings into the middle of the cross-section, still blank, as the voice says nothing reported says.

open_loop_2.what: Is the person with the AI helper an automated tool? Planted as the folded note pressing at the dashed edge under AUTOMATED TOOL = ?, carried through the middle caught half in the slot, seen from inside in shot 8 and behind the clerk in shot 11, paid in two moves, the ruler traces the edge solid under IF DEFINED NARROWLY, then on where a tool ends it breaks back into dashes, handing the question to the viewer.
